points.why: It sees diffuse, reasonable exceptions with no open opposition, but reads them mainly as goal erosion; it only hints at an unaccommodated real constraint at the very end.
It sketches a goal/gap/correction loop, but the target is the stated policy rather than an implicit coordination or response-time target that pulls meetings back.
It never suggests asking the people who book Wednesday meetings what they're protecting or where that expectation came from; it only proposes classifying meetings as internal or external.
Items 4 and 5 (fix why meetings can't move, resize the goal) point toward meeting or changing the target, but much of the advice adds enforcement pressure on the state.

pitfalls.why: It rejects a stronger re-announcement and explicitly says the policy didn't fail because people ignored it.

notes: Its core fixes (senior approval, public counts, making each exception owned by a person) push harder on the state without moving the underlying target, which the rubric predicts will meet the same pushback.
